{{Short description|Polygon with right angles and consecutive lengths}}
[[File:Octagon Golygon.svg|thumb|400px|The smallest golygon has 8 sides. It is the only solution with fewer than 16 sides. It contains two [[Concave polygon|concave]] corners, and fits on an 8×10 grid. It is also a [[spirolateral]], 8<sub>90°</sub><sup>1,5</sup>.]]
A '''golygon''', or more generally a '''serial isogon of 90°''', is any [[polygon]] with all [[right angle]]s (a [[rectilinear polygon]]) whose sides are consecutive [[integer]] lengths. Golygons were invented and named by [[Lee Sallows]], and popularized by [[A.K. Dewdney]] in a 1990 ''[[Scientific American]]'' column (Smith).<ref>{{cite journal |author=Dewdney, A.K. |title=An odd journey along even roads leads to home in Golygon City |journal=[[Scientific American]] |volume=263 |pages=118–121 |year=1990|doi=10.1038/scientificamerican0790-118 }}</ref> Variations on the definition of golygons involve allowing edges to cross, using sequences of edge lengths other than the consecutive integers, and considering turn [[angle]]s other than 90°.<ref>{{cite web |author=Harry J. Smith |title=What is a Golygon? |url=http://www.geocities.com/hjsmithh/Golygons/GolyWhat.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20091027155427/http://geocities.com/hjsmithh/Golygons/GolyWhat.html |archivedate=2009-10-27}}</ref>

== Properties==
In any golygon, all horizontal edges have the same [[parity (mathematics)|parity]] as each other, as do all vertical edges. Therefore, the number ''n'' of sides must allow the solution of the system of equations
:<math>\pm 1 \pm 3 \pm \cdots \pm (n-1) = 0</math>
:<math>\pm 2 \pm 4 \pm \cdots \pm n = 0.</math>

It follows from this that ''n'' must be a [[multiple (mathematics)|multiple]] of 8. For example, in the figure we have <math>-1 + 3 + 5 - 7 = 0</math> and <math>2 - 4 - 6 + 8 = 0</math>.

The number of golygons for a given permissible value of ''n'' may be computed efficiently using [[generating function]]s {{OEIS|id=A007219}}.  The number of golygons for permissible values of ''n''  is 4,&thinsp;112, 8432, 909288, etc.<ref>{{mathworld|title=Golygon|urlname=Golygon}}</ref>  Finding the number of solutions that correspond to non-crossing golygons seems to be significantly more difficult.

There is a unique eight-sided golygon (shown in the figure); it can [[tessellation|tile]] the plane by 180-degree rotation using the [[Conway criterion]].

==Generalizations==
A '''serial-sided isogon''' of order ''n'' is a closed polygon with a constant angle at each vertex and having consecutive sides of length 1, 2, ..., ''n'' units. The polygon may be self-crossing.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Sallows, Lee |title=New pathways in serial isogons |journal=[[The Mathematical Intelligencer]] |volume=14 |pages=55–67 |year=1992 |doi=10.1007/BF03025216 |issue=2|s2cid=121493484 }}</ref> Golygons are a [[special case]] of serial-sided isogons.<ref name=serial>{{cite journal |doi=10.2307/2690648 |author1=Sallows, Lee |author2=Gardner, Martin |author2-link=Martin Gardner |author3=Guy, Richard K. |author3-link=Richard K. Guy |author4=Knuth, Donald |author4-link=Donald Knuth |title=Serial isogons of 90 degrees |jstor= 2690648 |journal=[[Mathematics Magazine]] |volume=64 |issue=5 |year=1991 |pages=315–324}}</ref>

A [[spirolateral]] is similar construction, notationally ''n''<sub>&theta;</sub><sup>''i''<sub>1</sub>,''i''<sub>2</sub>,...,''i''<sub>''k''</sub></sup> which sequences lengths 1,2,3,...,''n'' with internal angles &theta;, with option of repeating until it returns to close with the original vertex. The ''i''<sub>1</sub>,''i''<sub>2</sub>,...,''i''<sub>''k''</sub> superscripts list edges that follow opposite turn directions.

<gallery>
serial isogon_9_120.svg|A serial-sided isogon order 9, internal angle 60°.<ref name=serial/><BR>[[Spirolateral]] 60°<sub>9</sub><sup>1,4,7</sup>.
Serial_isogon_11_60.svg|A serial-sided isogon order 11, internal angle 60°.<ref name=serial/><BR>[[Spirolateral]] 60°<sub>11</sub><sup>4,5,7,8</sup>.
serial isogon 12 60.svg|A serial-sided isogon order 12, internal angle 120°.<ref name=serial/><BR>Spirolateral 120°<sub>12</sub><sup>1,4,8</sup>.
Serial isogon 5 60 120.svg|A serial-sided isogon order 5, internal angles 60° and 120°.<ref name=serial/>
</gallery>

=== Golyhedron ===
The three-dimensional generalization of a golygon is called a '''golyhedron''' – a closed [[simply-connected]] solid figure confined to the faces of a cubical lattice and having face areas in the sequence 1, 2, ..., ''n'', for some integer ''n'',
first introduced in a MathOverflow question.<ref>[https://mathoverflow.net/q/164588/6094 "Can we find lattice polyhedra with faces of area 1,2,3,…?"]</ref><ref>[https://cp4space.wordpress.com/2014/04/30/golygons-and-golyhedra/ Golygons and golyhedra]</ref>

Golyhedrons have been found with values of ''n'' equal to 32, 15, 12, and 11 (the minimum possible).<ref>[https://cp4space.wordpress.com/2014/05/11/golyhedron-update/ Golyhedron update]</ref>
